findings.where: Footer links 'Privacy', 'Terms' and 'Report content', and the nav's 'Destinations' link (desktop nav and the phone menu)
findings.fault: These links look and act like links but go nowhere useful. Privacy, Terms and Report content all point back to this page. Destinations points to #destinations, and this page has no section with that name. A visitor who taps any of them stays where they are, with nothing to say why.
findings.who_objects: A backpacker checking how their data is handled, or trying to report a listing, gets nothing on tap. A dead Privacy or Terms link on a page whose whole job is trust tells a sceptical visitor the site is unfinished. The founder would object too, because the page is meant to prove the platform is honest and complete.

findings.where: Lede ('This page states it in full: how a hostel's position is decided') against the 'Ranking method' section
findings.fault: The page promises to explain how a hostel's position is decided, but it never says what the results are ordered by. It says what does not count (payment, partner tier, review count as the default sort). It never says whether the list is sorted by score, by distance, or by something else, or how ties are broken. 'Area' is also never defined.
findings.who_objects: A traveller who came here to check whether the top result earned its place leaves without knowing what put it there. They can see what was ruled out, but not what was used. The h1 and lede make a promise the page does not keep, and that weakens the trust the page exists to build.

findings.fault: The page names Hostelworld and describes its scoring as making hostels 'look thin', then ends on that competitor instead of on Manta's own method. PRODUCT.md says the demand-side claim 'names no competitor' and that Manta never competes on Hostelworld's ground. The Hostelworld consent question (#78) is also still open.
findings.who_objects: The founder would object: a public, competitor-naming comparison breaks the stated positioning and risks the pending Hostelworld relationship. A visitor would also feel the page closing on a jab at a rival rather than on what Manta does, which reads as marketing, not method.

findings.where: 'Ranking method' section (four paragraphs) against the 'Scoring method' section
findings.fault: The content sits under the wrong headings. 'Ranking method' holds four separate topics with no subheads: payment independence, scores pulled toward the area average, review filtering and badges, and default sort. Two of those are about how a score is calculated. 'Scoring method' holds only time decay. On a phone this becomes one long wall of text under a heading that doesn't match much of it.
findings.who_objects: A visitor scanning for one answer, such as 'are reviews filtered?' or 'why is this new hostel's score near the average?', can't find it by heading. They have to read every paragraph, often on a phone mid-trip.

findings.where: Body copy throughout, worst in the Hostelworld paragraph (one sentence of about 70 words) and in 'Both would bury exactly the low-review properties that pulling thin scores toward the area average exists to rank fairly'
findings.fault: Many sentences are long and tangled, nesting clauses inside each other, so the method is hard to follow even though each fact is plain on its own.
findings.who_objects: Backpackers, often reading in a second language on a phone in transit, would give up partway through. A method that is published but can't be followed earns less trust than a short one people can read.

findings.where: Intro block: the lede, the second intro paragraph and the three-point list
findings.fault: The page's strongest trust claim, 'No hostel can pay for a higher position', appears only as a small item in a plain list, in the same type as the body text. Two intro paragraphs come before it and take the visual weight. At a glance, nothing on the first screen stands out as the main point. The list is also numbered although its points are not steps or a ranking.
findings.who_objects: A visitor who arrives sceptical and skims for five seconds would miss the one line that answers their main doubt. The founder wants that line to land as the page's claim.

findings.fault: The page is one narrow column of text on plain sand, pushed to the left, with about 700 px of empty space on the right. There is no turquoise, no illustration and no brand moment between the nav and the footer. It reads as a bare legal document.
findings.who_objects: The founder would object: the brief names sterile and corporate as the enemy and asks for a loud claim with calm mechanics beneath it. This page has only the calm half. A visitor gets no sense of the brand's warmth on the page meant to win their trust.

findings.where: Whole page, and above all the intro
findings.fault: The page gives no date for the method and no 'last changed' line. The only date is when the Hostelworld source was read.
findings.who_objects: A visitor deciding whether to trust the ranking can't tell whether the method described is current. PRODUCT.md's 'rankings and scoring methods are published' only builds trust if readers know the published version is the one in use.
